item.title: 'State-led discrimination': Turkey jails 16 people after raids in Izmir on LGBTQ+ groups
item.description: Turkish police on Sunday arrested at least 60 people in mass raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ activists, in what authorities said was an operation aimed at boosting traditional family values. The raids sparked condemnation from rights groups and opposition parties, as well as the European Union parliament's rapporteur on Turkey. France 24’s Jasper Mortimer has the latest. item.title: A 'complicated autumn' awaits Sweden after knife-edge vote
item.description: Sweden's general election remained too close to call early Monday, with nearly 90 percent of votes counted. Four opposition parties led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson held a one-seat parliamentary lead over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing bloc, which includes the Sweden Democrats, as both leaders said they were ready to govern. item.description: Indonesia’s president sacked his finance minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa on Monday and replaced him with his deputy Suahasil Nazara, as he battles to win back investor confidence amid long-festering concerns about policymaking and fiscal profligacy. item.description: A predominantly Muslim region in the southern Philippines held its first parliamentary elections on Monday, seen as a crucial step in the long quest for self-rule after decades of insurgency and violence. item.title: Centre-left holds narrow lead in knife-edge Sweden vote
item.description: Sweden's centre-left opposition on ​Monday looked the most likely to form the next government as preliminary election results showed it holding a narrow three-seat lead over the right-wing ruling parties with most of the votes counted after Sunday's vote. item.description: Las autoridades turcas adelantan operativos contra la comunidad LGBTIQ+. En el marco de la "Operación mi familia está a salvo", la policía ha iniciado redadas en varios bares y discotecas de la comunidad, ha cerrado y bloqueado cuentas de redes sociales de defensores de derechos .y detenido a algunos activistas. item.description: Este domingo el presidente norteamericano volvió a mencionar la más conflictiva resultante del acuerdo del Viernes Santo, que puso fin a la guerra civil religiosa entre civiles y protestantes en Irlanda del Norte, con la mediación —entre otros— de Estados Unidos: la posibilidad de una Irlanda unida.
